question: Should Microsoft Teams adopt this hybrid root-default plus named-account inheritance model as its durable public multi-account configuration contract?
rationale: Implementation review can verify internal consistency, but maintainers must choose whether root inheritance, setup promotion, and named-account identity requirements are the intended long-term user contract.

options.title: Adopt hybrid contract
options.body: Retain root-level single-bot compatibility and allow named accounts to inherit shared non-identity settings.

options.title: Require account-only config
options.body: Move all bot settings beneath `accounts` and provide a doctor migration from the shipped root-level shape.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Keep the canonical feature issue open while a smaller or different account contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Adopt hybrid contract
recommendation.body: Retain root-level single-bot compatibility and allow named accounts to inherit shared non-identity settings.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the requested reviewer and has recent merged history across the setup, credential, authorization, and security-sensitive Teams surfaces involved.
